To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

language is an under-researched but important element of multinational team culture and performance and that task indicative cues are a key element of language that may be important to the development of shared team cultures and team performance.
the use of task indicative language in the shared language of the work team is a strong status cue in multinational teams.

The differential use of task-indicative cues spoken in a common language by multinational team members has the potential to influence team member status perceptions and, in turn, the performance of the team.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the differential use of language across multinational teams.
the differential use of language in multinational teams.
how language use can be used to create a shared team culture in a multinational team.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
language is a powerful status cue and, in multinational teams, the use of a shared language is a key element of team performance.
the use of language is a key factor for the success of multinational teams.
language is an integral component of the work performance of international teams.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
language choices in multinational teams are not just about language.
a shared language is not necessarily a shared language.

the use of a shared language by multinational teams is not necessarily the panacea for team performance, but that the differential use of language in the shared language is likely to have significant consequences for team performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a shared language is not a given, but rather a choice that can be used strategically to enhance or inhibit team performance.

the language choices that multinational team members make are not neutral, they are not simply the result of a shared language, and they do have implications for the performance of multinational teams.
language use can act as a status cue in multinational teams.
